claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially has a single-phase, high-temperature BCC structure.
The high-temperature BCC phase in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is metastable at lower temperatures.
The thermodynamic driving force for transformation from BCC is relatively weak because the alloy contains only 7 at.% Al.
An FCC or ordered phase is thermodynamically favored over BCC at lower temperatures.
Sluggish atomic diffusion in the multicomponent matrix counterbalances the thermodynamic driving force for transformation.
Rapid cooling kinetically preserves the high-temperature BCC state.
Annealing at approximately 700–900 °C provides sufficient atomic mobility for Al redistribution.
Annealing produces localized Al segregation or short-range ordering, potentially at grain boundaries or particular lattice planes.
Al redistribution and ordering lower the alloy free energy.
The free-energy reduction caused by Al ordering initiates transformation away from BCC.
Rapidly quenched samples will retain a uniform BCC structure.
Slowly annealed samples will contain small FCC or ordered precipitates together with residual BCC.
The annealing-induced precipitates will be associated with detectable local Al segregation.
The transformed-phase fraction will increase with annealing duration.
At temperatures below the proposed annealing window, negligible diffusion will suppress transformation.
At temperatures above the proposed annealing window, full equilibration may occur.
Temperature- and composition-dependent phase evolution, including ordered intermetallic formation at lower temperatures, occurs generally in Al-containing high-entropy alloys.
The controlled comparison uses samples from one batch, with a rapidly quenched condition as the baseline and an approximately 800 °C annealing series as the intervention.
Absence of both annealing-induced phase change and Al segregation, or comparable changes in the quenched baseline, is specified as falsifying the proposed mechanism.
